_library.edition: FreeCAD_FastenersWB at commit fddd07af422b7d3a69098b32333711c5eeae184c: the nominal lengths each standard offers, inside the per-size Min_L and Max_L of the same commit
_library.source: FreeCAD_FastenersWB FsData '<STD>length' and '<STD>range' sections, combined as ScrewMaker.GetAllLengths() combines them

_provenance.answer_to_does_the_source_carry_offered_: YES for every screw/bolt standard extracted, and NO for ISO 7089 (a washer has no length). FreeCAD_FastenersWB does NOT store an explicit per-size list. It stores two real tables and the workbench combines them at runtime: a '<STD>length' section holding the nominal lengths the standard offers, and a '<STD>range' section holding per-size Min_L and Max_L. ScrewMaker.GetAllLengths() emits exactly the nominals that fall inside [Min_L, Max_L]. The lists below are that computation reproduced verbatim - they are the lists the workbench itself offers, NOT an invented arithmetic series. Both inputs are also published per size (range_min_max_as_published_*) so the derivation can be checked.

no_offered_lengths_for.reason: washers carry no length/range table (correctly - a washer has no length)

boltsparts carries no offered-length table for this class. It does carry a 'common' block listing commercially common lengths for M3-M10 only, reproduced below under 'boltsparts_common_lengths_not_a_standard_range' - that is a shop-availability hint, not a standard's offered range, and no such data exists at all for M12/M16/M20.
no rows extracted at all (see standards.json)

observed_gaps_in_the_upstream_nominal_li: FsData/inch_fs_length.csv jumps 1/2in -> 3/4in -> 1in and omits 5/8in, 5/16in and 1 1/8in, so those never appear in an inch offered list.
FsData/asmeb18.2.1.6def.csv's own ASMEB18.2.1.6length list omits 3/4in, so the 1/2in and 5/8in sizes - whose Min_L IS 3/4in - start at 1in in the derived list.
Transcribed as-is; no nominal was added to fill a gap.
ASMEB18.3.3Arange and ASMEB18.3.1Grange are read from two different files: the button head's range sits beside its own def table, the low head's sits in asmeb18.3.1adef.csv.
